newsitem.title: USA: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- N.J. $2.8 bln deal priced.
newsitem.headline: U.S. MUNICIPAL FOCUS -- N.J. $2.8 bln deal priced.

text.p: U.S. municipal bonds slipped 1/8 to 1/4 point by midday, while new issue action saw the New Jersey Economic Development Authority price a $2.8 billion global deal.
"Our read on the bonds was that it was very well subscribed for," a trader at one firm said.
"I think they got a very good price," he said. "I think the state should be very happy."
Both traders' firms were among the 15 listed on the preliminary official statement for deal. Merrill Lynch & Co was senior manager.
Back in the secondary, prices were down 1/8 to 1/4 point in sympathy with government market softness, a trader said. Treasuries opened lower amid U.S. dollar weakness, he said.
"...Durable goods was just kind of within what people expected so it didn't really do anything, and then home sales were a little bit stronger than people expected," he said.
The Commerce Department reported that May durable goods orders fell 0.6 percent, compared to an upwardly revised 1.8 percent for the month. Economists had expected a 0.6-percent rise.

Later, the National Association of Realtors said existing home sales rose 4.4 percent in May to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of 4.24 million units from 4.06 million units in April. Economists expected the May figure to be 4.07 million units.

In the government market, the benchmark 30-year bond was off its lows but down 6/32 at 98-30/32 to yield 6.71 percent. In debt futures, the September municipal contract was down 2/32 at 117-10/32. The September T-bond contract ws down 5/32 at 112. The MOB spread was 170 ticks.
While muni cash prices were lower Wednesday, the outlook appeared improved compared to Friday and Monday, one trader said.

"Friday and Monday were kind of ugly in munis, but it really kind of stopped midday yesterday I think, and selling slowed down," the trader said. "I think we have the deals out of the way this week, people have got a holiday week next week, and they are just kind of hanging out."
As for new issues, municipal bond sales Wednesday are expected to total $4 billion in 35 deals, including the $2.8 billion New Jersey deal.

That offering is split between a fixed-rate tranche worth $1.3 billion and 28 zero-coupon bonds totaling $1.5 billion. The $1.3 billion fixed-rate bond has a legal final maturity of February 15, 2029, and has an expected average life of 29.855 years. It is to be priced at 66 basis points over the 6.50 percent November 2025 U.S. Treasury.
The 28 zero-coupon bonds have consecutive maturities from one-year to 29 years, but exclude a two-year bond.
